findings.evidence: `pathLaw_eq_bind_infinitePi_of_mixedIIDWith` at line 67 assumes only `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`, while `Measure.ext_of_bind_infinitePi_eq` at `MeasureTheory/Measure/MixtureInjective.lean:119` requires only `[IsFiniteMeasure π₁]`; Mathlib provides `Measure.isFiniteMeasure_map` for mapping any finite measure.
findings.fix: Replace it with `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`, instantiate `IsFiniteMeasure (μ.map ν)` using `Measure.isFiniteMeasure_map _ _`, and revise the docstring to distinguish finite from infinite base measures.
findings.issue: `[IsProbabilityMeasure μ]` is too strong; only finiteness is needed, contrary to the preceding claim that probability normalization is load-bearing.

summary: The uniqueness theorem unnecessarily restricts the base measure to a probability measure; its proof and dependencies work for every finite measure.
